title: Would you play a text-based life simulator set in China?
author: Yuewen1216
selftext: I'm an ordinary college student from China, and I'm currently using AI and learning "vibe coding" to build my first game project. I want to design a text-based game about simulating and experiencing the whole life of an ordinary Chinese person.  The game will have text choices that decide your career, marriage, and children, allowing players to feel how the future changes. I also want to design some unique Chinese cultural features, like the exam-oriented education system (Gaokao), the "liquor table" culture (social drinking rules), and things like that. The presentation style willbe similar to a Japanese galgame/visual novel.  I don't know if this is a good idea.What do you guys think?

comments.author: syn_krown
comments.body: I think you should ask in the interactive fiction subs. Leave out the AI part though lol

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
Honestly, this wouldn't be interesting to me unless it was set as period piece with kung-fu. 

I wouldn't really be interested in Japanese life sim, Korean life sim or American life sim either though.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: I personally don't think there are really that many people looking for text adventures at all.

replies.author: syn_krown
replies.body: Especially now that there are so many AI ones that can play out any kind of fantasy

comments.body: Ordinary life choices? No matter how hard you try, the game will be trivial and boring. Not to mention that you don't have life experience.

replies.author: Yuewen1216
replies.body: I agree with your point, but I still plan to give it a try.

comments.author: DuckAndQwack
comments.body: I wouldn't play/se anything from/in China, to be honest. Your country is quite dictatorship, kills people, colonies the poor countries, doesn't follow the international laws, support drug dealers, so I won't use/support anything from it. Games aren't "outside from the politics".

comments.author: Yuewen1216
comments.body: Thanks for all the feedback! I understand text-based life sims are a niche market, and I appreciate the pointer to the Interactive Fiction community. As a student developer, I'll focus on refining the core mechanics and cultural elements. Thanks again!
